raw_case_text:
The patient was a 35-year-old African American female with a history of asthma and polysubstance abuse who presented to the emergency department (ED) with severe shortness of breath. She reported that the shortness of breath was progressive over several months and associated with weight loss. She denied a history of HIV infection. The patient's only known home medication was albuterol as needed for asthma. She also reported a history of smoking 10 cigarettes a day and drinking alcohol a couple of times a week.
On physical examination, she was cachectic, ill-appearing and tachypneic with the use of accessory muscles for respiration. Her blood pressure was 88/55 mm Hg, temperature was 37.4 C, pulse rate was 146 beats per minute and regular, oxygen saturation of 70% on room air, and body mass index of 18.9. Lung auscultation revealed bilateral rhonchi. Heart auscultation revealed normal S1 and S2 without significant murmurs or rubs. She was placed on a non-rebreather mask with FiO2 of 100% without improvement of respiratory status and was switched to non-invasive mechanical ventilation. Her status continued to decline, and she underwent endotracheal intubation within an hour of arriving at the ED for hypoxic respiratory failure. SARS-CoV-2 testing done upon arrival in the ED was negative. She tested positive for HIV, and further evaluation revealed an initial viral load of 343,636 copies per milliliter and an absolute CD4 count of 5 cells/muL.
On day 1, a chest radiograph (Figure 1(a)) revealed extensive right lung opacities, most prominent in the right middle lobe. The cardiac silhouette was slightly enlarged. A chest CT scan with intravenous contrast (Figure 2) revealed severe cavitary and partially necrotic opacities in the right upper lobe. There was also a small right pleural effusion and a moderate pericardial effusion. An echocardiogram (Figure 3) revealed a large pericardial effusion, as large as 4.16 cm, with no signs of tamponade.
Initially, she was placed on vancomycin, cefepime, azithromycin, anidulafungin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SXM) and methylprednisolone. She also required norepinephrine and vasopressin for the first 5 days for hypotension, most likely due to septic shock. On day 5, she underwent bronchoscopy for BAL after tuberculosis was ruled out with three negative sputum acid-fast bacillus smears and a negative polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test. Chest radiography on day 8 (Figure 1(b)) revealed an increase in the right-sided infiltrates and new patchy infiltrates at the left lung base.
On day 13, PCR of the BAL was positive for CMV with CMV DNA of 197,000 IU/mL. Fungal culture of the BAL fluid did grow Candida albicans, which was determined to be a colonization. All other tests performed on the BAL (summarized in Table 1) were negative. Additionally, tests for Cryptococcus antigen, Histoplasma antigen, Legionella antigen, A. Galactomannan antigen and (1,3)-beta-D-glucan were negative. She was started on IV ganciclovir 250 mg twice a day for CMV pneumonia and antiretroviral therapy for HIV. Anidulafungin, methylprednisolone and all other antibiotics were discontinued except for TMP/SXM, which was continued for Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia (PJP) prophylaxis. She was extubated on day 13 and switched to high-flow nasal cannula. 
On day 17, a follow-up echocardiogram showed that she still had a large circumferential pericardial effusion that had not changed significantly in size since the day of admission. Pericardiocentesis was performed, draining 500 mL of straw-colored fluid. Pericardial fluid analysis was positive for CMV DNA using PCR and negative for adenosine deaminase. All other tests performed on the pericardial fluid (summarized in Table 1) were negative.
A chest radiograph on day 22 (Figure 1(c)) showed reduced infiltrates in the right lung field, with a moderate overlying pleural effusion. Her HIV viral load had decreased to 5,522 RNA copies per milliliter. She was breathing comfortably on room air. She was discharged on oral valganciclovir 900 mg twice a day until her CD4 count improved to over 100 cells/muL, TMP/SXM for PJP prophylaxis and Biktarvy as antiretroviral therapy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old African American female with asthma and polysubstance abuse presented to the emergency department with several months of progressively worsening shortness of breath and weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to the emergency department in severe respiratory distress after several months of progressively worsening dyspnea and unintentional weight loss, requiring endotracheal intubation within 1 hour of arrival after failing 100% FiO2 non-rebreather mask and noninvasive ventilation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Asthma; polysubstance abuse; active tobacco smoker (10 cigarettes/day) and alcohol use twice weekly; previously undiagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS discovered in the emergency department.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for progressive shortness of breath over several months and weight loss. Only home medication was inhaled albuterol as needed.

objective.physical_examination: Emergency department vital signs and anthropometrics: Blood pressure 88/55 mmHg, temperature 37.4 °C, regular tachycardia at 146 beats/min, room-air SpO2 70%, and cachexia with BMI 18.9 kg/m2. Physical exam: Ill-appearing, tachypneic with accessory respiratory muscle use; bilateral rhonchi on lung auscultation; normal S1/S2 without murmurs or rubs.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission virological and microbiological screening: Positive HIV test with initial plasma HIV viral load of 343,636 copies/mL (decreasing to 5,522 copies/mL by day 22); negative SARS-CoV-2 test; three negative sputum AFB smears and negative MTB PCR; negative Cryptococcus, Histoplasma, and Legionella antigens. Serial chest radiographs: Day 1 CXR showed extensive right lung opacities (most prominent in the right middle lobe) and cardiomegaly; day 8 CXR showed progression of right-sided infiltrates and new patchy left basilar infiltrates; day 22 CXR showed marked clearance of right lung infiltrates with a residual moderate right pleural effusion. Echocardiograms (days 1 and 17): Large circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 4.16 cm without cardiac tamponade.
objective.advanced_workup: Immunological and fungal biomarkers: Profound CD4+ T-cell depletion with absolute CD4 count of 5 cells/μL; negative serum Aspergillus galactomannan and negative (1,3)-beta-D-glucan. Contrast-enhanced chest CT (day 1): Severe cavitary and partially necrotic opacities in the right upper lobe, small right pleural effusion, and moderate-to-large pericardial effusion. Day 5 bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL; results returned day 13): Positive quantitative CMV PCR with BAL CMV DNA load of 197,000 IU/mL and Candida albicans colonization on fungal culture; negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii, bacteria, mycobacteria, and endemic fungi. Day 17 therapeutic pericardiocentesis (draining 500 mL straw-colored fluid): Pericardial fluid PCR tested positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV) DNA and negative for adenosine deaminase (ADA) and other pathogens.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Newly diagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4 count 5 cells/μL, viral load 343,636 copies/mL) presenting with necrotizing cavitary right upper lobe cytomegalovirus (CMV) pneumonia and large CMV pericardial effusion (confirmed by BAL CMV DNA of 197,000 IU/mL and positive pericardial fluid CMV PCR, with Pneumocystis jirovecii and tuberculosis excluded by negative BAL studies, AFB smears/PCR, and negative serum beta-D-glucan). Plan and clinical course: Intubated in the ED and supported for the first 5 days with norepinephrine and vasopressin alongside empiric vancomycin, cefepime, azithromycin, anidulafungin, therapeutic TMP/SMX, and methylprednisolone. On day 13, upon BAL confirmation of CMV pneumonia and exclusion of PJP, she was extubated to HFNC, switched to intravenous ganciclovir (250 mg twice daily), prophylactic-dose TMP/SMX, and antiretroviral therapy (bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide [Biktarvy]), and underwent pericardiocentesis (500 mL) on day 17. She was discharged on room air on day 22 on oral valganciclovir (900 mg twice daily until CD4 >100 cells/μL), prophylactic TMP/SMX, and Biktarvy.
